clue.text: Celestial body that holds it's wicked, say, to exaggerate

indicators.note: the comet holds the next piece within its own letters, so it acts as the container

parts.note: a comet is a celestial body with a glowing tail
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: say signals that the word before it is spoken, and only its sound is entered

parts.note: wicked means wrong, which is spoken here and entered by its sound

explanation.surface: An astronomer describes a heavenly body that is supposedly evil, in overblown language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's wicked, say' reads like a judgement on the comet; in fact 'holds' is the container and 'say' makes only the last piece a sound-alike, spelt without its W.
explanation.definitionFit: To come it strong is an old idiom for laying it on thick, overstating things.

clue.text: Horse he puts down to expenses

definitions.meaning: someone who bills an item to an account

explanation.surface: A rider claims the cost of their mount on expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhorse is called this; also one who bills a cost to an account.

clue.text: Who's buried at Corunna? A Spanish conqueror, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard rather than read, so only its sound is entered

parts.note: the Moors conquered most of Spain in the eighth century

explanation.surface: A history quiz asks about a grave in Galicia and offers a Moorish invader.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Moore, the British general, died at the Battle of Corunna (1809) and was buried there.
explanation.definitionFit: The general killed and buried at Corunna in the Peninsular War bore this surname.

clue.text: In Asian country, start to climb a hill — this shows the way

indicators.note: In tells us the next letter is placed inside the country's name

parts.note: India is a country in south Asia

indicators.note: start to climb means the first letter of climb

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A traveller in India sets out to climb a hill and asks for directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link but is the container signal; a tor is a craggy hill of southwest England, as on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer or signpost is something that tells you which direction to go.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: a verb here: to stop a flow, as of blood
the stalk that holds up a flower or leaf

explanation.definitionFit: To stop a flow is to stanch it; a plant's stalk holds up its leaves and flower.

clue.text: Sound rebound?

definitions.meaning: dependable, as in a sound investment
read as re-bound, bound again, that is, under an obligation once more

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits 'rebound' as RE (again) plus 'bound' (obliged, liable).
explanation.definitionFit: Something sound can be depended on; and being liable again means re-obliged.

clue.text: 24 metamorphosed into a spirit of nature

indicators.note: metamorphosed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 24, the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: A goddess is transformed into a woodland sprite, as in Ovid.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 24-down supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph, a minor nature deity of springs and rivers.

clue.text: Saw a pilot with the George medal

parts.note: PO is short for pilot officer, an RAF rank
taken as written
GM is the abbreviation for the George Medal, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: An airman is decorated with the George Medal for gallantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the tool or the past tense of see but a noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a proverb, a pithy maxim, as is this word.

clue.text: Method of keeping Surrey's boundaries down to 4

indicators.note: boundaries are the edges, so the first and last letters of the county name

parts.note: the answer to 4-down, a plant's stalk

explanation.surface: A cricket club in Surrey plans how to tend its boundary ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY is a county south of London; its first and last letters are S and Y, then the answer to 4-down follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure or scheme for doing something is a synonym.

clue.text: Many a bargain

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a large quantity, and also a favourable transaction.

clue.text: Suggest I am to go to and fro

parts.note: contracted to I'm
ferries ply, travelling regularly back and forth

explanation.surface: Someone hints that they are to commute back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without stating it outright is a synonym.

clue.text: By the sound of it, the fat of the land

indicators.note: the phrase signals that a word is heard, and a different spelling is entered

parts.note: grease is animal fat

explanation.surface: The phrase recalls living off the fat of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fat of the land' is a stock phrase for the best of everything, which hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean country is a land, a nation.

clue.text: Out east listened to a bird beavering away

indicators.note: out tells us a letter leaves the word for listened

parts.note: listened means heard
E is the compass abbreviation for east
the tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone listened to birdsong out east while toiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' removes E from HEARD to leave HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Working industriously, like a busy beaver, is this idiom.

clue.text: Hogwash devoured in turn

parts.note: rot means nonsense
devoured means ate

explanation.surface: Pigswill is gobbled up by each animal in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin round an axis is a synonym of revolve.

clue.text: Model worker for a while unpunctual

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
unpunctual means late

explanation.surface: An agency model who works temporarily never arrives on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern used as a guide for copying is a synonym.

clue.text: Dogfight

parts.note: split as dog plus fight: a breed of spaniel and a 1704 battle share the name

explanation.walkthrough: It is a toy spaniel breed and Marlborough's victory of 1704; the one word holds both.
explanation.definitionFit: The palace and battle name also labels a small red-and-white spaniel.

clue.text: Sat in gaol unhappily thinking of the past

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things are out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner sat in jail, wistful and sad about better days.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful longing for earlier times is the noun's sense.

clue.text: Who interrupted an auction en masse?

indicators.note: the question word breaks into the auction phrase, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: an auction is a sale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bidder asks which crowd burst in on an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken all together, collectively, is the meaning.

clue.text: Form P.C. 19 makes a mess of

indicators.note: making a mess of something jumbles it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: PC is police constable
the answer to clue 19, a chemistry term

explanation.surface: A police constable bungles an official form.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up or constitute something, as parts form a whole, is a synonym.

clue.text: Did he write for the yellow press?

definitions.text: Did he write for the yellow press?

parts.words: Did he write for the yellow press?
parts.note: yellow is slang for ..., so the clue seeks a playwright whose surname means someone lacking courage

explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward wrote plays, not tabloid journalism; the yellow press means sensational newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright's surname also denotes a timid person, one with a yellow streak.

clue.text: One of similar compounds — I'll: get a few right

parts.note: I'll gives the letter I
some means a few

explanation.surface: A chemist promises to get a few compounds right.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule with the same formula as another but differently arranged atoms is the term.

clue.text: End wearing torn clothing

indicators.note: the tear wears the aim, so it contains the next word

parts.note: rent means ripped
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Ragged clothes are worn out at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' reads as 'dressed in' to suit the clothing picture, but it is the container signal: the torn word wears the end word.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for garments and attire.

clue.text: Clue to wolf, or maybe duck?

parts.note: wild suggests rearranged letters, so ... reads as instructions that make wolf from fowl

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks about a wolf or a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a clue, 'wild fowl' would be an anagram of FOWL, giving WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: A duck is a game bird, one example of this group.

clue.text: Treat with contempt noisy oaf

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a lout is a boor

explanation.surface: A rowdy oaf is treated with scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn a rule or convention openly is a synonym.

clue.text: A participant in fighting and hitting people? Yes and no.

indicators.note: participant in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone joins in brawling and striking others, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the joke: Gandhi led people in struggle but refused to hit anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of non-violent resistance fought for his people but never struck a blow.

clue.text: Girl could turn up as an auxiliary

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: an aid is an auxiliary or helper

explanation.surface: A girl may appear as a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A common given name for a woman, as with the Roman goddess.

clue.text: Pole is nuts

definitions.meaning: the upright spar of a ship
fallen beech and oak nuts, used as pig feed

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's spar is one sense; fallen beech or acorn crop is the other.

clue.text: Proportion of army retreating into city

indicators.note: into places the army piece inside the city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city

indicators.note: retreating means moving back, so the army abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: Part of the army retreats into a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve; 'retreating' turns its abbreviation round before 'into' places it in the Brazilian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantitative relation between two amounts is the term.

clue.text: Agreed on a recipe for drink

indicators.note: a recipe mixes ingredients, so the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: People agreed on how to make a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy citrus soft drink.

clue.text: Very different institute, in which. engineers stick around

indicators.note: in which means the next pieces sit inside the word for institute

parts.note: to institute is to start
RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: around signals that the word for stick is read backwards

parts.note: paste means glue

explanation.surface: An institute where engineers stick around is unlike any other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'institute' is a verb here, to begin; 'around' turns the glue word backwards, and 'in which' sets the engineers and that piece inside it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things far removed from each other are this idiom.
